chapter: Learning trombone and the Wisconsin Roof years
title: The Sims band's Savoy job and the trip to Lansing
summary: After the Wisconsin Roof they played the Savoy and drove to Lansing, with a car breakdown in Miami, Oklahoma.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: He'd play music, he'd trance all across the street. It was a novelty, you know. A dancing chicken? Well he'd strut kind of like he was dancing, you know. You could call it a dancing rock. So after that we stayed around Chicago, I mean Milwaukee, and gave our own dances. We would just draw away from the Wisconsin roof, where we was popular, we had been there six years. There was two bands there, Bill Costner's band. Well we wasn't allowed to play any waltzes. We could. But this other band was more on the street or the street, you know. They didn't play jazz as well as we did. Because then we got Zill and Randolph taking a mouse-randolph place, later on the mouse played with Cal Calaway. And Zill was the guy that was the music director for Louis Armstrong. He wrote this old man Moses day, you know. And so then we opened up in the Savoy in Chicago, three nights a week. And we left there and we went down to Tulsa. Then we jumped from Tulsa to, we thought it was going to be a little interesting place to call Miami, Oklahoma. We were on our way to a long jump from Tulsa to Lansing, Michigan. So we, just outside of Miami, a woman kept, she had one of these T models. We had three cars. We had a Whippet, Willis Knight, and a Buick. And she just, it was cutting right sharp across us, you know. And so our bad luck to leave this battery, we had a Willis Knight that split wide open. So when we made it into Miami, a crowd gathered there, you know. And so they began to keep calling going. Well, there's a fellow right across the street. He had a large garage and he said, you fellas come on in. He said, look like you may get in some trouble. So he drove all the way to Joplin, Missouri and obtained a battery and came back and said, you know. And so they told us, don't let dark kick you. But when darkness came, we ate them clay, the red clay. We was in Joplin. So, and then we couldn't get in to eat, sing to eat. Then we went on to St. Louis and we ate. And then we finally made it up to Lansing. So I stayed with him about two or three weeks. And then Dave Payton had the band at the Regan.
